subject: Discrepancy: proration across billing window causing token delta
messages:
From: Emma Lowe <emma@lumenai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: LumenAI Finance <finance@lumenai.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy in May usage export — sessions spanning billing boundary

Hi Rafael,

We just reviewed our May invoice (Inv #LU-202705) and noticed a ~27% delta between our internal token accounting and the usage CSV you provided earlier: your file shows 349,872 tokens billed, while our logs show ~275,430.

Quick summary of what we observed on our side:
- Several long-running sessions from May 1 that stayed open across midnight UTC and continued the next morning.
- We aggregate by session_id and attribute tokens to the session start date; that puts ~46k tokens into April on our side.

Could you share a session-level export or confirm how Redwood proration works when a session spans a billing boundary? Specifically:
- Do you ever attribute the same session slice to both days (double-counting) when stream reconnections occur?
- How are partial-session tokens prorated if a session started in April but has activity in May?

I've attached our export (May_usage_export.csv) and a short example of two session_ids with timestamps. If you can point us to the exact session rows that caused the 74k difference, we can reconcile quickly.

Would appreciate a response by EOD tomorrow — finance has placed the invoice on hold pending clarification.

Thanks,
Emma Lowe
Sr. Finance Ops
LumenAI

Attachments: May_usage_export.csv (text/csv, 24KB)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lowe <emma@lumenai.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in May usage export — sessions spanning billing boundary

Hi Emma — thanks for flagging this and for the sample rows.

Looping in Naomi from Billing and Marissa (your account lead) to triage. Naomi — can you pull a session-level extract for LumenAI for the May 1–3 window and check for any proration or duplicate attribution around midnight UTC? I suspect this could be related to reconnections and our stream-stitch logic that marks session fragments.

Proposed next steps:
- Naomi to confirm whether any known proration rounding or duplicate attribution occurred (ETA: 24–48h).
- If there is an over-bill, we can propose a pro-rated credit on the June invoice or a standalone credit note earlier if needed.
- Schedule a 30-min sync with Emma and their finance team if the CSVs don't reconcile.

Emma — could you also send a pair of session_ids that you think are the clearest examples? That will speed things up.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Manager, Customer Finance
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Lowe <emma@lumenai.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in May usage export — sessions spanning billing boundary

Thanks for looping me in. I pulled a session-level metering extract for LumenAI covering 2027-04-30 00:00:00 UTC through 2027-05-03 23:59:59 UTC (attached: metering_extract_202705.csv). Preliminary findings:

- Root cause (likely): when a client performs a streaming reconnect within an active session and the reconnection occurs after the UTC midnight boundary, our session-stitch logic created two fragments that were both counted in the May bucket due to a later reconciliation job failing to merge them. In short, some session fragments were not merged back to the original session_id before daily aggregation.
- Impact: ~72,410 tokens were attributed to May that should have been split to April; this matches the delta Emma reported within noise.
- Temporary mitigation: we already patched the reconciliation job on 2027-05-11 (fixed idempotency bug) and reprocessed 05/01–05/02; new aggregates reduced apparent overcount for a sample tenant by 98%.

Recommendation:
- Provide LumenAI a one-time credit of 72,410 tokens equivalent at their bill rate (we can convert to USD on the invoice line).
- Issue a corrected usage CSV and an explanatory note.
- Apply the same patch retroactively for other tenants on request; we will proactively scan for similarly affected accounts over the month.

Attachments: metering_extract_202705.csv (text/csv, 48KB)

Let me know if you want me to prepare a credit memo draft and timeline (I can have that ready today).

—Naomi
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Emma Lowe <emma@lumenai.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in May usage export — sessions spanning billing boundary

Thanks Naomi — that explanation makes sense and aligns with what we see. We had the call this morning with Marissa and Rafael and reviewed the reprocessed extracts.

A couple of quick asks to finalize:
- Please send the corrected usage CSV and the proposed credit amount in USD so our accounting team can release the invoice (we prefer a credit note on the current account rather than separate refund).
- Can you confirm when the credit will appear on our June statement? Our month-end close is June 5 so earlier is better.
- Attached a zipped bundle of our raw session logs for your QA team in case anything else is needed (client_session_logs.zip).

We appreciate the quick patch and the proactive reprocess. Please include the HubSpot ticket reference HS-452198 on the credit memo.

Best,
Emma Lowe
Sr. Finance Ops, LumenAI

Attachments: client_session_logs.zip (application/zip, 2.1MB)
